metadata.title: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis of DNA
metadata.purpose: Separate double-stranded DNA fragments by size in an agarose gel and visualize them under UV light using an intercalating stain, sized against a co-run DNA ladder.
metadata.scope: Analytical horizontal agarose gel electrophoresis of dsDNA in 1x TAE or TBE with ethidium-bromide staining. Pulsed-field electrophoresis and preparative band recovery are out of scope.
beforeYouBegin: Choose the agarose percentage based on the size of the fragments to be separated.
Use the same running buffer in the gel and in the tank.
Handle ethidium bromide and UV light as hazards (gloves; UV eye/skin protection).

materials.specification: Tris-acetate-EDTA (TAE) or Tris-borate-EDTA (TBE); use the same buffer in the gel and the tank

samples.name: DNA sample(s) to analyze

tables.title: Run parameters (Addgene quick-reference)
tables.note: All values from the Addgene Gel Electrophoresis protocol.

steps.action: Weigh agarose and mix with 1x TAE or TBE to the chosen percentage (0.7-2% by fragment size).

parameters.rawText: 0.7% to 2% depending on the size of bands needed to be separated

steps.action: Melt the agarose in a microwave until completely dissolved.

parameters.rawText: Microwave for 1-3 min until the agarose is completely dissolved

steps.safetyNotes: Molten agarose and the flask are very hot; swirl carefully to avoid superheating/boil-over.

steps.action: Cool the molten agarose to about 50 C, then add ethidium bromide to 0.2-0.5 µg/mL and swirl to mix.

parameters.rawText: about 50 °C (about when you can comfortably keep your hand on the flask)

steps.criticalNotes: Wear gloves; ethidium bromide is a mutagen.
steps.expectedResult: Stained molten agarose ready to pour.

steps.action: Pour the agarose into the casting tray with a comb and let it solidify.
Remove the comb, place the gel in the tank, and add 1x buffer to cover the gel.
steps.criticalNotes: Use the same buffer as in the gel.
steps.expectedResult: Gel submerged and ready to load.

steps.action: Mix each DNA sample with loading dye (5 µL per 25 µL sample) and load samples and a DNA ladder into the wells.

parameters.rawText: Use 5 µl of loading buffer per 25 µl of sample

steps.criticalNotes: Load the ladder in a dedicated lane to size the sample bands.

steps.action: Run the gel at 80-150 V until the dye front has migrated an appropriate distance.
steps.criticalNotes: Lower voltage / longer run improves resolution of similarly sized bands.
steps.expectedResult: DNA migrated and separated by size.

steps.action: Visualize the DNA under long-wavelength UV and photograph the gel.
steps.safetyNotes: UV damages eyes and skin - use a face shield / UV-blocking screen.
steps.criticalNotes: Long-wave UV is recommended to minimize DNA damage.
steps.expectedResult: Fluorescent DNA bands, sized against the ladder.

controls.name: DNA size ladder
controls.description: Molecular-weight marker run in a dedicated lane to size sample bands.

expectedOutputs: Discrete DNA bands resolved by size, sized against the co-run ladder.
A UV gel image documenting fragment sizes.

troubleshooting.cause: Too much DNA loaded; run too fast/hot; degraded DNA
troubleshooting.solution: Load less DNA; run at lower voltage; use fresh/intact DNA

troubleshooting.cause: Stain omitted; DNA ran off the gel; too little DNA
troubleshooting.solution: Confirm stain was added; shorten run/monitor dye front; load more DNA

troubleshooting.cause: Agarose % not matched to fragment size
troubleshooting.solution: Use a higher % for small fragments, lower % for large fragments; run longer at lower voltage

safety: Ethidium bromide is a mutagen - wear gloves and dispose of gels and buffer as hazardous waste.
UV light damages eyes and skin - use a face shield or UV-blocking screen.
Molten agarose and its container are hot - handle with heat protection.
limitations: Analytical horizontal agarose electrophoresis; resolution and agarose percentage depend on the fragment size range. The UV wavelength is not numerically specified in the source (long-wave UV, typically ~365 nm). For fragments <100 bp or >20 kb, or for preparative recovery, use specialized methods.
